stem: Which situation contributed to the problem described in this excerpt?

options.label: F
options.text: Migration caused by racial discrimination during World War I

options.label: G
options.text: Homelessness caused by unemployment during the Great Depression

options.label: H
options.text: Strict bank regulations made by the federal government during the New Deal

options.label: J
options.text: Rate increases imposed by the railroad industry during the Gilded Age

visual_elements: The Federal Children’s Bureau, in the summer of 1932, undertook a survey of the situation in the Southwest, with especial reference to boys and young men who by the thousands (estimated 200,000 for the United States) were found “riding the rods” of the railroads. . . . In October 1932 a group of individuals, members of national agencies deeply concerned with this problem, together with a number of persons actively engaged in the study of the subject, organized themselves under the auspices of the National Social Work Council as a discussion group to explore the size and content of the problem . . . and, if possible, to work out some practical plan for its relief. —Dr. Ellen C. Potter, "The Problem of the Transient," 1934
